Om. The Dharma, characterized by qualities such as invisibility, is declared. Om. 1/2/21.

The qualities such as invisibility are declared to be those of Vishnu. There, after stating, “That which is invisible and ungraspable,” and then stating, “Just as the web is spun and gathered by the spider, just as plants arise from the earth, just as hairs and body hair arise from a living being, so does the universe arise here from the Imperishable,” it is inferred that the Supreme (Para) is distinct from the Imperishable (Akshara). Therefore, it was declared: “The Dharma, characterized by qualities such as invisibility, is declared.” After citing the analogy of the earth and stating, “The universe arises here from the Imperishable,” the subsequent reference to “That which is beyond the Imperishable” (tat-paratara) leads to the understanding of Prakriti, as per the memory (smriti) that “The Unchanging (Kutastha) is called the Imperishable (Akshara).” Furthermore, Hiranyagarbha is understood from the term “Brahman” and the reference to “That which is beyond the Imperishable.”

By the statements beginning with, “One who knows Him thus becomes immortal here,” “That action is the delight of Hari; that is the knowledge, that is the thought by which...,” and “Now, two kinds of knowledge are to be known: the higher (para) and the lower (apara). That which consists of the Vedas, their limbs, sub-limbs, and inner limbs is the lower. But the higher is that by which Hari is to be known, who is that invisible, attributeless, Supreme Self beyond the Supreme,” the subject matter of the higher knowledge (para-vidya), whose nature is Dharma, is understood to be Vishnu alone, characterized by qualities such as invisibility. 21.
